about:
The Food Innovation Center operates in Portland, Oregon, as one of Oregon State University's Agricultural Experiment Stations. Established as a university-based service center, it provides technical, creative, and educational support to the food industry, entrepreneurs, and communities across the Northwest. The center houses the Western Regional Center to Enhance Food Safety (WRCEFS), one of four U.S. regional centers created to coordinate food safety training under the Food Safety Modernization Act.

The center delivers a range of services including product development and formulation from benchtop through pilot scale, shelf-life studies on finished products, nutrition labeling, sensory and consumer testing, and process authority services such as thermal process approvals. It also provides FSMA-focused training workshops for small and medium-sized farms, beginning farmers, socially disadvantaged farmers, and small processors. Consulting services cover economic analysis, community development, and market readiness research.

Clients span the food and beverage manufacturing sector, agricultural producers, and early-stage food entrepreneurs. The center works directly with small fresh fruit and vegetable merchant wholesalers, specialty food processors, and ingredient suppliers seeking formulation support or regulatory guidance. Its outreach extends to 13 western states and two territories through the WRCEFS sub-regional network.

The center was built to address gaps in food safety training and product commercialization for smaller operators. Its mission emphasizes quality, safety, and sustainability, aiming to reduce food waste and drive innovation funding across the regional supply chain.
